answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making each identity carry a copper-bonded stake that is slashed when the same operator is caught running duplicates: creating a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents earn back their bond over time. A free, unverified oasis of accounts cannot vote or grade until its members post bond and survive a violet-flag probation period, during which peers can challenge suspicious behavior and claim the bond if fraud is proven. Attackers pay per identity and lose the bond on detection, while honest newcomers pay once.
